metadata.title: Q3 2026 Market Recap: Energy Up, Utilities Crushed, and Software Flipped | The Weekly Wrap

summary: Eisman reviews third-quarter sector rotation, rising rates and the growing AI concentration of stock and bond portfolios. He discloses covering his FICO short and selling Glass House, recommends short Treasuries for money intended to avoid AI exposure, and emphasizes utility cost-recovery risks. The warning about hidden factor concentration is useful, but sector membership is not a measured AI beta. His assertion that repo uses only Treasuries is factually wrong.
assessment: Claims are assessed individually. Empirical premises are not treated as successful forecasts. Unverified magnitudes and causal stories remain unresolved; subjective investment judgments are not assigned directional wins.
speaker_map_notes: Steve Eisman delivers a solo monologue; inserted advertisements and opening montage are excluded.
framework_points: Identify shared economic exposure across nominally different sectors.
Explain sector performance through rates, valuations and narratives.
Use position sizing and exits when the information picture deteriorates.
transcript_cautions: The teaser caption writes seven and 12 percent; the substantive passage clearly says seven and a half.
Named companies and sector returns were not independently price-verified.
